# Contributing

<!-- Generated by scrum-github (preset environments). Edit it freely: init never overwrites it. -->

## Branches

| Branch | What it holds | Who writes to it |
|---|---|---|
| `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` | Released code (production). Every version tag (`{{TAG_PREFIX}}1.2.0`) is on this branch. | Release and hotfix pull requests only |
| `{{STAGING_BRANCH}}` | Code under test before a release. | Promotion pull requests from `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`, back-merges from `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` |
| `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` | Work that is done but not promoted yet. | Pull requests from task branches |
| `feat/<task>-<slug>`, `fix/...` | One task. Created from `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`. | You |
| `hotfix/<task>-<slug>` | An urgent fix of a released version. Created from `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`. | You |

Code moves one way: task branch → `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` → `{{STAGING_BRANCH}}` → `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`. Only `hotfix/*` starts
from `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`. Nobody pushes to the long-lived branches directly: every change goes through a pull
request, which needs the required checks and the review.

## Pull requests

- Target `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`. `{{STAGING_BRANCH}}` accepts only `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` (a promotion) and `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` (a back-merge);
  `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` accepts only `release/*` and `hotfix/*`. Any other pull request fails the source-branch check.
- The title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org): a type (`feat`,
  `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, `perf`, `build`, `revert`), an optional scope,
  `!` for a breaking change, then `: ` and a summary. Example: `feat(auth): log in with email`.
- The description closes its task: `Closes #<task number>`. A change without a task gets the
  `{{NO_TASK_LABEL}}` label instead.
- Squash-merge task pull requests into `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`. Promotions, releases and back-merges are merged with
  a merge commit, never squashed.

A task merged into `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` stays In review with the label `{{LOCATION_PREFIX}}{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`, then `{{LOCATION_PREFIX}}{{STAGING_BRANCH}}` once
promoted; it is Done when its code reaches `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` in a release.

## Promotion and releases

1. `/scrum-github:promote` opens the promotion pull request `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` → `{{STAGING_BRANCH}}`.
2. `/scrum-github:release` opens a release pull request from `release/<tag>` into `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` with the
   version, the release notes and the updated version files.
3. Review it and merge it with a merge commit. The release workflow then creates the tag and the
   GitHub Release, sets the released tasks Done and opens the back-merges into `{{STAGING_BRANCH}}` and
   `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`.
4. Merge the back-merge pull requests with a merge commit.

A hotfix: `/scrum-github:hotfix <task>` creates `hotfix/<task>-<slug>` from `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`; its pull request
targets `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` and publishes a patch version when merged.{{DEPLOY_SECTION}}
